solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gossip from poor player

definitions.meaning: British slang for chattering at length
in British sport a ... is a weak, inept player, especially a tail-end batsman

explanation.surface: Idle talk overheard about some hopeless performer on a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are British informal usage: chattering away, and a feeble sportsman.

clue.text: Monarch's circling island on covering local area

indicators.note: the royal word goes round the island and on pieces

parts.note: regal means belonging to or befitting a king or queen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A king encircling an island, his power extending over a district.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional describes something relating to or spanning a particular district rather than the whole country.

clue.text: Objection at university outside the Italian town

indicators.note: the objection word sits outside the Italian article

parts.note: 'but' introduces or names an objection, as in no ifs or buts
il is Italian for the
to be up is to be in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A student raising a protest about the Italian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Built-up describes an area covered in buildings, so 'town' as an attributive noun stands for urban development.

clue.text: Unchanging in verse, song's not without heart

parts.note: taken as written
an aria is a solo song in opera

indicators.note: the middle letter of the negative is removed

explanation.surface: A poem's song lacking passion, never varying in tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Invariant means constant, never varying, which is exactly unchanging.

clue.text: Recalled line, a quote linked to work of verse

indicators.note: called back, so the run of pieces from line to work is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to quote a passage is to cite it
OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A line of poetry remembered and quoted alongside some literary piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns LACITEOP right round, giving the whole answer; 'linked to' merely joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetical is an adjective meaning relating to or written in poetry, which is what 'of verse' says.

clue.text: Arranged proper cut in production of eggs in excess numbers

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go in the egg-release word

parts.note: ovulation is the release of eggs from the ovary

indicators.note: arranged means put in a fresh order, so the shortened letters are reordered
the word proper is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: Planned culling within egg-laying to deal with overcrowding, perhaps of poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' looks like a past-tense verb opening the story, but it is the signal to reorder the shortened letters; 'cut' trims just one letter from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Overpopulation is having more people or animals than an area can support, too many in number.

clue.text: Body, scientific body, that's brought in as well

indicators.note: the academy letters are brought into the also word

parts.note: too means also, as well
RS is the Royal Society, Britain's national academy of sciences

explanation.surface: A learned society that is admitted into something too.
explanation.definitionFit: A torso is the trunk of the human frame, the main part of the body without head or limbs.

clue.text: Oppose prisoner getting trial

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A convict about to face trial plans to fight the charges.
explanation.definitionFit: To contest a claim or decision is to dispute or challenge it, a synonym for oppose.

clue.text: Parking spaces — store last of trolleys here!

parts.note: to lay by is to put aside for later use, to store

indicators.note: the final letter of the trolleys word is taken

explanation.surface: A supermarket sign telling shoppers to leave the final trolleys in this car park.
explanation.walkthrough: A lay-by is a British roadside pull-in for stopping vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay-bys are areas beside a road where drivers can pull over and stop their cars.

clue.text: Nice at sea, with one navy assembled around, having put out

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the gathered word sits around the mixed-up city letters

parts.note: convened means gathered together for a meeting

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the city's letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A naval fleet gathering offshore near Nice, having been sent out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective; 'at sea' signals that its letters are jumbled, and 'around' has the meeting word enclose them.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put out is to be bothered or caused trouble, which is what inconvenienced means.

clue.text: Nice grave vandalised, leading to complaint

indicators.note: something vandalised is smashed up, so the letters of the two place and tomb words are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Desecration of a tomb in the French city of Nice provokes a formal protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like an adjective but is the city, its letters joining GRAVE in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievance is a formal complaint or a cause for one, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Highly-sexed extremes of rumpy-pumpy?

parts.note: the outermost letters of that word are ..., spelt out with the joining word between them

explanation.surface: Asks whether frantic bedroom antics at their wildest show someone highly sexed.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of 'rumpy-pumpy' are R and Y; write that phrase out in full, conjunction included. Rumpy-pumpy is British slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Randy is informal British for lustful or sexually eager, a direct synonym for highly-sexed.

clue.text: Working with chamber group, going round a province

parts.note: a machine that is working is on

indicators.note: the musical group goes round, enclosing the single letter

parts.note: a trio is a chamber ensemble of three musicians

explanation.surface: A busy chamber ensemble touring a region of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' sets A inside TRIO, after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario is a Canadian province, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Children supplying zero information in probe

indicators.note: the zero and information pieces are placed in the snooping word

parts.note: to pry is to probe or snoop
the figure nought looks like the letter O
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Kids providing nothing useful when questioned by an investigation.
explanation.definitionFit: Progeny means offspring, the children or descendants of a person, so it fits as a plural noun.

clue.text: Peak hour activity initially getting highest rating

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain peak

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the two following words

explanation.surface: Rush-hour activity at the start achieving top marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peak hour' reads as rush hour, but 'Peak' stands alone as ALP.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the top grade in some marking schemes, as in alpha plus, so it means the highest rating.

clue.text: Velocity and pace with no initial lack of content

parts.note: V is the symbol for velocity in physics

indicators.note: the speed word loses its first letter

parts.note: rapidity is speed, a synonym for pace

explanation.surface: Speed without substance: going fast but empty-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: Vapidity is dullness or emptiness of ideas, an absence of substance or interest.

clue.text: Chipped dish and religious book in sack

indicators.note: a chipped item has lost a bit, so the plate word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
a missal is a book of Mass prayers

explanation.surface: A damaged plate and a prayer book thrown into a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' looks like a bag, but it is the definition: firing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the sack is being fired, and dismissal is the removal of someone from their job.

clue.text: Line dances, overlooking daughter's attempt

indicators.note: overlooked means left out, so the dancing word drops a letter

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter, as in genealogy
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A dance formation in a row, ignoring a girl's go at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line dances' reads as one phrase; 'Line' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A line is a family's lineage, the descent from forebears, which is what ancestry means.

clue.text: Soldier despatched on raid by the Spanish

parts.note: troops sent in are despatched into action, as on a raid
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A soldier dispatched on an assault alongside Spanish forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a sentry, a soldier posted to stand guard.

clue.text: English literature is primarily too exclusive?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first of all, so the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Wondering whether studying English literature is a bit snobbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitist describes favouring a select group, being snobbishly selective about who belongs.

clue.text: Go out in the near future to embrace women

indicators.note: the time word hugs the letter for women

parts.note: soon means in a short while
W is the abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors

explanation.surface: Planning to head out shortly and hug some women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go out' suggests leaving the house; here it means losing consciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoon is to faint, and to go out is an informal way of saying lose consciousness.

clue.text: Unusual volume in very short time turning up, following regular delivery?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the whole construction from bottom to top
the rare and volume pieces go in the brief-time word

parts.note: mo, short for moment, is a brief interval
rare means unusual

explanation.surface: A book rarely delivered by a postal round, coming quickly after the usual post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses MRAREVO in full. In cricket the usual bowling action is overarm, with the arm swung above the shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: Overarm bowling is the standard style in cricket, so it is a normal delivery, the question mark flagging the sporting sense.

clue.text: Not enlightened over everything in Chinese food

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: dim means dull-witted or poorly lit
the sum is the total, everything

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by everything on a Chinese menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim sum are small Cantonese dumplings and snacks, a style of Chinese cuisine.

clue.text: Copy the very thing required to intervene in one game's conclusion

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the needed-thing piece steps in between the other letters

parts.note: mate, or checkmate, ends a game of chess
'it' means exactly what is needed, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: Mimicking exactly what is needed to break into a match's final moments.
explanation.walkthrough: IT goes into IMATE after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to copy someone's behaviour or manner, so the verbs match.

clue.text: A desire to skip party? Here's an excuse

indicators.note: skipping means missing out, so the party word is dropped from the desire word

parts.note: libido is sexual desire
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Fancying giving a party a miss and offering a reason.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is an excuse or claim of being elsewhere, used informally for any pretext.

clue.text: Boat engineers needed after stern lost in journey

indicators.note: the stern is the back of a vessel, so the journey word loses its final letter

parts.note: a trip is a journey
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A vessel needs mechanics after its rear end comes off mid-voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: Most solvers try RE for 'engineers'; here it is the full Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers abbreviation. 'needed after' fixes the order.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme is an ancient galley with three banks of oars, an example of a boat.

clue.text: Selection of books offering some terrific stories, on reflection

indicators.note: reflected as in a mirror, the run is read backwards
only some of the letters of the two words are taken, a run spanning them

explanation.surface: A batch of novels with some great tales, thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: The run IFICS from 'terrific stories' is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sci-fi, science fiction, is a genre, so a shelf or section of such novels in a library or shop.

clue.text: It's corn, as manufactured for breakfast item

indicators.note: something manufactured is made up, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cereal-company slogan: corn processed to make your morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests cornflakes; the apostrophe in 'It's' gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A croissant is a crescent-shaped pastry eaten in the morning, an example of something on a breakfast table.

clue.text: Curtailed article in post reaching US lawyer, a woman

indicators.note: the shortened article goes in the post word

parts.note: mail and post both mean letters delivered

indicators.note: having its tail cut off, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: 'the' is the definite article
a DA is a District Attorney, an American public prosecutor

explanation.surface: A shortened item in the post reaches an American attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtailed' means docked of its tail, the last letter, rather than reduced in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathilda is a woman's name, so a girl's or woman's name serves as the definition by example.

clue.text: I'm second in race — not very strong at all

indicators.note: the two pieces go in the racing word

parts.note: to fly is to rush or race along
taken as written, the apostrophe giving no letter

explanation.surface: A runner admitting coming second shows they are hardly powerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Flimsy means weak and insubstantial, easily broken or torn.
